variations.name: Triple-pane and passive-house-grade windows and frames
variations.description: Three glass panes plus thermally broken, airtight frames roughly halve window heat loss versus standard double-pane units, removing the weakest element of the building envelope; standard in Europe and now pushed in the US by ENERGY STAR 7.0 and IRA incentives.

companies.name: Alpen High Performance Products
companies.what: Colorado maker of thin-glass triple/quad IGUs and ultra-efficient fiberglass windows that hit passive-house performance at lower weight
companies.signal: $18M raise Jun 2024 anchored by $5.9M DOE grant; factory expansion adding ~100 jobs

companies.name: Zola Windows
companies.what: Boutique Colorado supplier of European-made Passive House-certified wood, uPVC and aluminum windows for high-end North American projects
companies.signal: Supplying NA passive-house custom market since 2008

companies.name: Intus Windows
companies.what: Volume supplier of European-style triple-pane uPVC windows for US multifamily, including Sendero Verde, the world's largest residential Passive House project
companies.signal: One of the largest European-style window suppliers in North America; PHIUS-verified Supera line

companies.name: Cascadia Windows
companies.what: BC-based manufacturer of fiberglass triple-glazed windows and the first fiberglass window-wall system for mid-rise construction
companies.signal: Universal Series Window Wall won 2024 Architizer A+ Product Award

companies.name: Internorm
companies.what: Austria's family-owned window giant where triple glazing is the standard product across the entire range
companies.signal: Europe's leading premium window brand; tens of millions of units produced

companies.name: Schüco
companies.what: German facade and window systems house supplying high-performance aluminum and uPVC frame systems to fabricators worldwide
companies.signal: Multi-billion-euro revenue; global spec leader for commercial fenestration systems

companies.name: Andersen Windows
companies.what: Largest North American window maker, now offering triple-pane options across mainstream lines and investing in glazing startups (was an Ubiquitous Energy investor)
companies.signal: ~$3B revenue; triple-pane moving into volume residential with ENERGY STAR 7.0

variations.name: Vacuum-insulated glazing (VIG)
variations.description: Two panes separated by a sub-millimeter evacuated gap deliver wall-like center-of-glass insulation (R-10 to R-18) in a unit thin and light enough to drop into existing sashes, enabling deep window retrofits without replacing frames.

companies.name: LuxWall
companies.what: Michigan startup making Enthermal R-18 VIG and operating the first high-volume US VIG plant
companies.signal: $51M Series B Nov 2024 (Climate Investment, Barclays); Litchfield MI plant opened Aug 2024; second Detroit plant part of $165M, 450-job Michigan buildout; Breakthrough Energy-backed

companies.name: NSG / Pilkington
companies.what: Maker of Spacia, the first commercial VIG (Japan, 1997), sold globally for slim heritage retrofits
companies.signal: 25+ years of commercial VIG production

companies.name: AGC (Fineo)
companies.what: Runs a purpose-built Belgian plant making pump-port-free Fineo VIG aimed at monument and heritage window retrofit
companies.signal: Dedicated Brussels-area facility; 20-year warranty product sold across Europe

companies.name: Vitro Architectural Glass
companies.what: North America's largest glassmaker, bringing tempered VacuMax VIG production onshore via an exclusive agreement with VIG Technologies/LandVac
companies.signal: Exclusive long-term NA manufacturing and licensing agreement signed Nov 2025

companies.name: LandGlass (LandVac)
companies.what: Leading Chinese producer of fully tempered VIG with the lowest U-values on the market, now licensing technology westward
companies.signal: Lowest U-value among major VIG products per independent comparisons; tech behind Vitro's VacuMax

companies.name: Panasonic
companies.what: Adapted plasma-display vacuum tech into Glavenir VIG and now sells complete turnkey VIG manufacturing lines to European and North American glass factories
companies.signal: Triple-pane-beating performance in a 6-8mm unit; pivoted to equipment-line sales model

companies.name: V-Glass
companies.what: Wisconsin startup with a hermetic metal-seal VIG design targeting cost parity with conventional IGUs (50-75% below first-gen VIG cost)
companies.signal: $3M seed led by Grantham Foundation plus $1M ARPA-E GLASING award (Mar 2026); moving from lab to pilot plant; NREL-tested panels

variations.name: Electrochromic and other electrically dynamic smart glass
variations.description: Glazing that tints on demand under a small applied voltage (electrochromic, SPD or liquid-crystal), cutting cooling loads, glare and blind usage while preserving views — commercially proven for a decade but capital-heavy manufacturing bankrupted the first generation of pure-plays in 2024.

companies.name: View Inc.
companies.what: Built the largest dedicated EC fab (Olive Branch, MS) and the highest-profile smart-glass brand for US commercial real estate
companies.signal: Consumed well over $2B (incl. $1.1B SoftBank) and SPAC'd in 2021; Chapter 11 Apr 2024 wiped equity; emerged private May 2024 under lender/Cantor Fitzgerald- and RXR-linked ownership

companies.name: Halio (formerly Kinestral)
companies.what: Made fast-switching, color-neutral EC glass with fabs in California and Taiwan
companies.signal: ~$564M raised over 11 rounds, incl. $70M from SKC in late 2023; became insolvent and shut down in H1 2024

companies.name: SageGlass (Saint-Gobain)
companies.what: The only smart-glass maker owned by a global building-materials group; produces EC glass at its Faribault, MN plant
companies.signal: Wholly owned by Saint-Gobain since 2012; commercial production since 2013; still actively selling worldwide as of 2025-26

companies.name: Miru Smart Technologies
companies.what: Vancouver startup making low-cost EC windows on existing glass-coating infrastructure, including the world's largest compound-curved EC sunroof for vehicles
companies.signal: C$27.4M Series A Aug 2024; US$5M venture debt Feb 2025; first commercial purchase orders 2025; strategic equity from Mativ Jan 2026

companies.name: Tynt Technologies
companies.what: CU Boulder spinout using reversible metal electrodeposition so windows tint continuously to full blackout, replacing both low-e shading and blinds
companies.signal: ~$16M raised to date; Series A-II ($2.75M) Nov 2025; DOE-supported technology

companies.name: Glass Dyenamics
companies.what: Early-stage developer pitching lower-cost dynamic glass for residential price points
companies.signal: Small seed-stage venture; little verifiable public activity since ~2023

companies.name: ChromoGenics
companies.what: Swedish maker of ConverLight foil-based dynamic glass laminated by partner glassworks
companies.signal: Delisted from Nasdaq First North Sep 2024 amid ~30% staff cuts; continuing at reduced scale as of late 2025

companies.name: Gauzy
companies.what: Israeli maker of SPD and liquid-crystal smart-glass films for architecture and transport (aircraft, automotive)
companies.signal: Nasdaq IPO Jun 2024 raised $75M at ~$244M valuation; FY2024 revenue $103.5M (+33%); guiding $130-140M for 2025

variations.white_space: The 2024 collapse of View (>$2B consumed) and Halio ($564M) showed that dedicated EC fabs cannot survive construction-industry sales cycles; the opening is low-capex routes — retrofittable EC films, reversible-metal-electrodeposition chemistry, or licensing deposition onto existing float/coating lines — rather than another billion-dollar greenfield fab.

variations.name: Thermochromic and passive-dynamic glazing
variations.description: Interlayers or coatings that darken automatically as direct sunlight heats the glass, providing dynamic solar control with zero wiring, power or controls — a cheap alternative to electrochromics, at the cost of occupant control.

companies.name: Pleotint (Suntuitive)
companies.what: Michigan maker of the Suntuitive sunlight-responsive thermochromic interlayer, once billed as the world's most-adopted dynamic glass
companies.signal: Production and sales of the Suntuitive line suspended since the COVID era; suspension notice still posted in 2025, company says it hopes to return

companies.name: RavenWindow (RavenBrick)
companies.what: Denver startup that made thermochromic-filter retrofit windows switching at a set temperature
companies.signal: Raised VC and utility-partner funding in the 2010s; website and operations appear defunct since ~2020

variations.white_space: Effectively vacant after Pleotint suspended production and RavenWindow folded: passive tint tracks glass temperature rather than occupant intent (tinting on hot overcast days, lagging in winter sun) and offers no smart-building data story to justify premiums. The opening is commodity-priced thermochromic PVB bundled into standard laminating lines for hot-climate volume housing, where 'no controls' is a feature rather than a bug.

variations.name: Window inserts, secondary glazing and low-e storm windows
variations.description: A second sealed pane added inside or outside existing windows captures most of the energy benefit of full replacement at roughly a quarter of the cost, making it the highest-ROI fenestration retrofit — especially for historic buildings and the huge single-pane commercial stock.

companies.name: Indow
companies.what: Portland, OR maker of compression-fit acrylic interior inserts requiring no hardware, certified in standard and acoustic grades
companies.signal: AERC-certified for commercial use; claims ~20% heating/cooling savings and up to 70% noise reduction; widely used in historic preservation

companies.name: Larson Manufacturing
companies.what: Largest US storm-window maker; ComfortSeal low-e interior storm windows sold at big-box price points
companies.signal: Four low-e interior models AERC-certified; acquired by Fortune Brands in 2020 and still the channel leader

companies.name: Quanta Technologies (QuantaPanel)
companies.what: Pennsylvania maker of architectural low-e interior 'insulating glass systems' (600/700 series) that upgrade commercial and multifamily windows to near-replacement performance
companies.signal: ENERGY STAR and AERC certified; qualifies for federal retrofit tax credits; active through 2025

companies.name: Magnetite
companies.what: Long-running US/Australia franchise retrofitting magnetically attached acrylic secondary glazing over existing frames
companies.signal: Decades of installs across residential and commercial retrofit; active dealer network

companies.name: Alpen (WinSert)
companies.what: Sells WinSert thin-glass, low-e insert panels purpose-built for commercial window retrofits without replacement
companies.signal: DOE-backed thin-glass IGU capacity expansion ($18M, 2024) supports insert line

variations.white_space: Residential is well served, but commercial secondary glazing has only small players (Indow, Quanta) facing an enormous single-pane office stock under LL97-style carbon fines — the gap is scale-up capital, installer networks and financing models more than technology.

variations.name: Solar-control and low-e retrofit window films
variations.description: Thin polymer films with spectrally selective or low-e metal/ceramic coatings applied to existing glass reject a large share of solar heat (and, in low-e versions, retain winter heat) at a small fraction of glazing-replacement cost.

companies.name: 3M
companies.what: Inventor of much of the category; Prestige spectrally selective and Thinsulate low-e films that add roughly a pane's worth of performance to existing glass
companies.signal: Global market leader with decades of architectural film deployment

companies.name: Eastman (LLumar/SunTek/V-Kool)
companies.what: Owns the world's largest window-film brand portfolio spanning architectural solar-control and safety films
companies.signal: LLumar is the most widely distributed architectural film brand globally

companies.name: Madico
companies.what: Florida-based film maker (owned by Japan's Lintec) producing solar-control, safety and energy films
companies.signal: One of the oldest US film manufacturers, supplying global dealer networks

companies.name: Saint-Gobain (Solar Gard)
companies.what: Architectural and automotive solar-control films arm of the French materials giant
companies.signal: Sold in 90+ countries with documented carbon-negative product footprint claims

companies.name: Avery Dennison (Hanita Coatings)
companies.what: Israeli coater Hanita, acquired by Avery Dennison in 2017, makes SolarZone exterior-grade solar-control films popular for commercial retrofits
companies.signal: Integrated into Avery Dennison's global films business since 2017

variations.name: Transparent photovoltaic and energy-harvesting glazing
variations.description: Coatings or interlayers that convert ultraviolet/infrared light (or edge-routed visible light) to electricity while remaining see-through, turning windows and facades into generators — physics limits output to roughly 5-50 W/m², so economics remain hard.

companies.name: Ubiquitous Energy
companies.what: MIT-spinout leader in truly transparent UV/IR-harvesting coatings (UE Power) targeting residential windows with partner Andersen
companies.signal: Raised >$70M incl. Andersen strategic round; furloughed then terminated staff Apr 2024; website offline since Sep 2024 — effectively ceased operations

companies.name: ClearVue Technologies
companies.what: ASX-listed Australian firm whose glazing routes light to PV cells at panel edges, used in vision glass, skylights and solar greenhouses
companies.signal: Gen3 product >50 W/m² (+66%) unveiled Sep 2025; $3M non-dilutive facility for certification; ASX:CPV

companies.name: NEXT Energy Technologies
companies.what: Santa Barbara startup printing transparent organic-PV coatings that glass fabricators can laminate into standard IGUs
companies.signal: $13.4M Series C Feb 2024 (investors include fabricator Viracon); produced world's largest transparent OPV window (40x60 in) and installed six full-size units at HQ in 2025

companies.name: Physee
companies.what: Dutch firm behind PowerWindow edge-PV glazing, since pivoted toward sensor-driven SmartSkin facade controls
companies.signal: EU pilot installations; current commercial traction of PV glazing unclear

companies.name: Onyx Solar
companies.what: Spanish maker of semi-transparent amorphous-silicon BIPV glass for facades, canopies and skylights — trading some transparency for real output
companies.signal: 500+ projects in 60+ countries incl. flagship US corporate campuses; profitable niche leader

variations.white_space: Physics caps fully transparent PV at tens of W/m², and Ubiquitous Energy's collapse despite Andersen's backing shows VC-scale economics don't close on vision glass alone; the viable openings are semi-transparent applications (spandrels, skylights, greenhouses, balustrades) where transparency can be traded for output, or licensing coatings into existing IGU lamination lines rather than building fabs.

variations.name: Automated exterior shading, screens and dynamic facades
variations.description: Motorized exterior venetian blinds, fabric screens and louvers intercept solar gain before it passes through the glass — cutting heat gain through windows by up to ~90% — making them the cheapest peak-cooling fenestration measure; standard in Europe, rare in North America.

companies.name: Warema
companies.what: Europe's market leader in external venetian blinds and sun-shading control systems with full building-automation integration
companies.signal: Architects' Darling Gold award 2025; family-owned German leader with hundreds of millions of euros in revenue

companies.name: Griesser
companies.what: Swiss maker of exterior lamella blinds and facade shading since 1882, dominant in the DACH spec market
companies.signal: 140+ years operating; core supplier for European low-energy buildings

companies.name: Renson
companies.what: Belgian specialist in tensioned fabric screens, structural louvers and ventilated facade systems
companies.signal: Major EU spec-market player exporting screen systems globally

companies.name: Somfy
companies.what: French maker of the motors, sensors and controls that power most of the world's automated blinds and shades
companies.signal: ~€1.5B annual revenue; de facto standard drive platform for shading OEMs

companies.name: Hunter Douglas
companies.what: World's largest blinds and shades maker, incl. insulating honeycomb shades (Duette) and PowerView automation
companies.signal: 3G Capital acquired 75% in Feb 2022 at ~$7.1B enterprise value; continues operating globally

companies.name: SolarGaps
companies.what: Ukrainian startup making sun-tracking exterior venetian blinds with PV slats that shade while generating power
companies.signal: ~$1.5M raised plus €1M EU Horizon grant; thousands installed; Kyiv factory operating through wartime, demand boosted by grid attacks

variations.white_space: Crowded and mature in Europe but structurally absent from North American volume construction — no installer base, hurricane/wind-code friction, and aesthetics resistance; an opening exists for a US-focused, code-compliant integrated window+exterior-shade product or utility-program channel, as DOE attachment studies show exterior shading beats most glazing upgrades on cost per ton of cooling.

variations.name: Daylighting systems: tubular skylights and diffusing panels
variations.description: Tubular daylighting devices and translucent diffusing panels pipe or spread natural light deep into buildings, displacing 20-60% of daytime electric lighting without the heat gain and leak risk of conventional skylights.

companies.name: Solatube International
companies.what: Category creator and worldwide leader in tubular daylighting devices with high-reflectance light-pipe optics
companies.signal: Acquired by Kingspan Light + Air (closed Dec 2021, announced Jun 2022); continues operating from Vista, CA under founder-era leadership

companies.name: VELUX
companies.what: World's largest roof-window and skylight maker, including Sun Tunnel tubular daylights and commercial modular skylights
companies.signal: ~€3B revenue Danish foundation-owned group

companies.name: Kalwall
companies.what: New Hampshire family firm making translucent FRP sandwich panels for facades/skyroofs, with aerogel-filled options reaching U-0.05 while diffusing glare-free light
companies.signal: In continuous production since 1955; spec standard for museum/athletic daylighting

companies.name: Kingspan Light + Air
companies.what: Kingspan division consolidating daylighting (CPI Daylighting, Solatube) plus smoke vents and louvers into one envelope offering
companies.signal: Serial acquirer building the daylighting category leader inside a ~€8B group

companies.name: Parans Solar Lighting
companies.what: Swedish maker of sun-tracking collectors that pipe sunlight through fiber optics up to ~100m into windowless interiors
companies.signal: Niche player (~5 employees) operating since 2003; technology proven but volumes tiny

variations.name: Transparent aerogel and super-insulating glazing inserts
variations.description: Monolithic transparent silica aerogel sheets (or translucent aerogel granule fills) placed between panes add wall-like R-value with almost no added weight or thickness, promising triple-pane performance in a double-pane form factor.

companies.name: AeroShield Materials
companies.what: MIT spinout producing optically clear monolithic aerogel sheets to slot inside standard double-pane IGUs and door glass
companies.signal: $14.5M ARPA-E SCALEUP award Jun 2024 plus $5M equity Jul 2024; 12,000 sq ft Waltham pilot plant opened 2024; commissioned one of the world's largest critical-point dryers Jan 2025; first door-glass units produced

companies.name: Cabot Corporation
companies.what: Makes Lumira translucent aerogel granules used as insulating fill in Kalwall, polycarbonate and channel-glass daylighting panels
companies.signal: Commercial for over a decade across daylighting panel partners

companies.name: Okalux (Glas Trösch)
companies.what: German specialty glazier whose OKAGEL aerogel-filled insulating glass delivers very low U-values with diffuse daylight
companies.signal: Long-standing specialty product line; part of Glas Trösch group since 2018

variations.white_space: Only a handful of players because supercritical drying of clear, crack-free aerogel monoliths is slow and capex-heavy at window sizes — transparency-grade optics is much harder than industrial aerogel blankets; whoever industrializes continuous or ambient-pressure drying for clear monoliths unlocks triple-pane performance retrofittable into the existing double-pane manufacturing base.
